summary.title: Messages found between girlfriend and her ex
summary.what_happened: While my girlfriend was in the shower, I looked through her phone. I know her code. I found messages between her and her ex. Most were normal, such as asking how he is and that his mum is sick. She had never told me they were in contact. One message said 'I miss talking to you like this'. We have been together two years. I have checked her phone a few times before when I felt insecure.
summary.my_feelings: I felt insecure before I looked. The message 'I miss talking to you like this' is what affected me most.
summary.my_needs: I have not said what I need beyond knowing about her contact with him.
summary.desired_outcome: I want to confront her tonight and show her screenshots of the messages.

consult.text:
It sounds like finding those messages, and that one line in particular, really shook you. It also makes sense that you wanted to know why she had not mentioned it.

Here is how she may see it. Much of what you described is ordinary: asking how he is, and talking about his mum being sick. She may have seen the contact as harmless, or as support for someone going through something hard. She may have kept quiet to avoid an argument, rather than to hide something. The line that bothered you could mean more than that, or less. You cannot tell from one message.

The main issue I see in how this goes from here is how you found the messages. You went through her phone without her knowing, and you said you have done it before. That is a serious breach of her privacy. If you confront her tonight with screenshots, the conversation will quickly become about that.

What you do not know is what she thinks the contact is, or whether she would have told you.

Some next steps. Wait until you are calmer than tonight. Start by telling her you looked at her phone. Then ask about the contact and listen before you decide what it means.
Don't make this about me checking her phone. She's the one hiding things.

I can hear that you feel hurt and want answers. Her not telling you is something you can raise, and I am not asking you to ignore it.

The point I would keep is that the phone is likely to come up whatever you do. If you start with screenshots, it may feel like a trial to her, and you may not get the honest answer you are after.

What may help is to start with what you did, in plain words. Then say that you saw the messages and that it hurt that you had not heard about the contact. Then ask her what it means to her. I can help you work out how to say that if you would like.
